title: Never deploy a raw Pod in Kubernetes. Do this instead
caption: Kubernetes Deployments explained in 40 seconds. How do you handle rolling updates in production?

scenes.vo: If a raw Pod crashes at three AM, nobody brings it back. A Deployment wraps your Pods so they stay alive forever.
scenes.heading: DEPLOYMENTS

scenes.vo: Think of a Deployment like a vending machine supervisor, constantly restocking snacks the moment one drops.
scenes.heading: THE SUPERVISOR

scenes.vo: You declare a desired count of three replicas. If one Pod fails, Kubernetes spots the gap and launches a replacement.
scenes.heading: DESIRED STATE

scenes.vo: Want to ship a new version with zero downtime? Update the image, and Kubernetes rolls out new Pods one by one.
scenes.heading: ROLLING UPDATE

scenes.vo: Deployments bring self healing, rolling updates, and effortless scaling. Follow for more Kubernetes in plain English.
scenes.heading: DEPLOYMENTS
